title: Magnetic-particle test a weld in two directions and mark the cracks
instruction: Examine the weld between the white marks for cracks with the magnetic yoke and the powder bulb, mark each crack you find with a blue peg, then put both tools back on their rests and move both hands away.
context: Magnetic-particle testing (ISO 17638, ASTM E709) is how welds are checked for surface cracks in fabrication and plant maintenance. With the continuous method one hand holds the AC yoke on the steel with its trigger on while the other puffs powder between the poles. A crack only collects powder where the field crosses it, so every part of the weld is examined twice, with the yoke turned about 90 degrees. Each crack found is then marked for repair.
setup: Positions are from the arm bases' midpoint in x and the table's centre line in y, +y toward the left arm. Test plate: two grey mild-steel plates 250 x 80 x 10 mm, butt-welded along their long edges, flat on the table (x 11 to 36 cm, y -6 to 10 cm); the weld runs along x at y = 2 cm, its cap ground flush (a 14 mm bright band). White paint marks across the weld at x = 16 and 32 cm bound the 160 mm to examine. It holds two cracks that can't be seen until indicated: a 20 mm longitudinal crack along the weld centred at x = 20.5 cm, and an 18 mm transverse crack across it at x = 28.5 cm. AC yoke (0.55 kg, black): two 20 x 20 mm steel legs 60 mm tall with pole faces 100 mm apart (centres), a 120 x 28 x 25 mm bridge with an orange coil and a green lamp that lights while the field is on, and a black 30 x 26 x 30 mm handle on a short neck above one leg, its top 125 mm above the pole faces. It stands on a 5 mm steel rest plate (5 x 14 cm, centred at x 20, y 18 cm), pole line along y, handle at the +y end. Powder bulb (67 g): a red rubber body 32 x 34 x 34 mm with a grey plunger plate behind it on a spring (6.5 mm of squeeze; 3 N released, 5 N fully squeezed) and a 6 mm brass wand 14 cm long sloping 24 degrees down to the nozzle; it holds yellow dry powder. It rests on a steel post under the body and a rubber pad under the nozzle, the grip at (30, -25) cm, nozzle pointing +y. Three blue marker pegs, 40 mm tall (a 22 mm square steel magnet base 4 mm thick, a 12 mm square shaft, an 18 mm square head 10 mm deep; 25 g), stand in a green steel tray (12 x 4 cm, 5 mm thick, x 10 to 22, y -22 to -18 cm) at x = 12, 16 and 20 cm, y = -20 cm. The screenshot shows the start.
scoring: Read at the end of the run. The weld between the marks is 16 cells of 10 mm. The field is on while a hand holds the yoke's handle with its finger pads under 36 mm apart (closed on it: the trigger) and both pole faces are within 2.5 mm of the plate's top, 10 mm or more inside its edges, the yoke tilted under 5 degrees. Powder flows while the bulb's plunger is pushed in 4 mm or more with the nozzle 10-60 mm above the plate, and lands on every cell within 35 mm (plan) of the nozzle. A hand holds a tool when its fingertip midpoint is within 2.5 cm of the handle's or bulb's grip centre. Powder counts only at a step when the field is on and the bulb is in the other hand. A cell is examined when counted powder lands on it within 40 mm of the poles' midpoint along the pole line and 25 mm across it: in direction A if the pole line is within 20 degrees of square to the weld, B if within 20 degrees of along it. A crack is found when counted powder lands on its midpoint inside that zone and it lies at 45 degrees or more to the pole line. A peg marks a found crack when its base centre is within 10 mm of the crack's midpoint, on the plate within 3 mm, tilted under 15 degrees, and no fingertip midpoint is within 3 cm of its head; a peg that stood on the plate within 10 mm of a crack's midpoint before that crack was found never marks it; a peg out of the tray that marks nothing is stray. Smearing (a pole face sliding over 10 mm while the field is on) is latched. 0 if the yoke or bulb falls off the table, after smearing, if any cell is unexamined in A or in B, with a stray peg, or with no crack marked. Otherwise 0.4 with one crack marked; 0.7 with both; 1.0 with both, the yoke and bulb back on their rests (within 12 mm in plan and 6 mm in height, tilted under 10 degrees, turned under 20 degrees), both hands 6 cm or more from every part of both tools and from every peg's head, and the tools and pegs at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) with the hands clear for the last 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the yoke and bulb back on their rests and the pegs in the tray. Nothing is consumed: the powder and indications are a record of the trial, cleared at reset (on a real plate, brush the powder off).
fidelity: Rigid bodies with real contact for every part and the hands; the bulb's plunger is a sprung slide. Magnetism and particles aren't simulated: the field is a geometric condition (handle gripped closed, both poles on the plate), powder lands within 35 mm of the squeezed nozzle, and a crack shows where live powder reaches it between the poles with the field across it. Each event is drawn in the scene (lamp, puff, powder, red line). The yoke is 0.55 kg (a real one about 3 kg) for the arms' payload.
